fills.researcher_notes: No source names a commissioning year for the PIPELINE itself, so this is the field-onstream-date proxy the protocol asks to flag explicitly. Two independent trade/reference sources agree the Sawan gas field (OMV-operated, Sindh) came on stream in 2003: Oil & Gas Journal, 'Compression to buoy Sawan gas output in Pakistan' -- 'OMV discovered Sawan in 1998. The field, declared commercial in December 1999 and put on stream in 2003, lies between the markets of gas suppliers Sui Northern Gas Pipelines [and SSGC]'; Wikipedia 'Sawan Gas Field' infobox -- 'Start of production: October 22, 2003'. This 24-inch Sawan-Qadirpur MAINLINE is the sole original trunk carrying that field's gas to the Qadirpur delivery point -- confirmed still current and unchanged by SNGPL's own asset register, 'TRANSMISSION SYSTEM As at June 30, 2018' (SNGPL Annual Report 2018, printed p.32, row 11): 'SAWAN - QADIRPUR / 24 / 131.00' km mainline -- an EXACT match to this row's LengthKnown (131.0) and Diameter (24), so this is unambiguously the right physical asset (verifier FAILs on this large 186-page/4MB PDF -- 'value not found' is the documented large-PDF false negative, not a real miss; manually confirmed via pdftotext -layout). SNGPL's separate Musharaka fixed-asset note in the same report ('24" Dia 81.42 Miles Sawan-Qadirpur Line', cost unchanged 2017/2018 at Rs 997,609 thousand, book value falling from Rs 154,629k to Rs 94,773k in one year) shows a mature, steadily-depreciating asset consistent with a ~2003 build, not a newly capitalized one -- corroborating context, not proof of the exact year. Given the gap between a field date and a pipe date, tier=low per protocol; a human may prefer StartYear1='2003 (inferred from Sawan field onstream date)' over a bare '2003'.  SEE ALSO the duplicate question below on P4101/SV1-QV1 -- resolved by the SAME asset register.

validity.recommendation: Do NOT merge or delete either P4079 or P4101 -- treat the brief's duplicate question as resolved in the negative. Keep both rows as distinct, real, parallel pipelines.
validity.researcher_notes: The brief flagged that P4079 (Sawan-Qadirpur, 24in, 131.0 km) and P4101 (SV1-QV1, 42in, 130.77 km) share both endpoints and might be the same line under two labels. SNGPL's own current asset register settles this: 'TRANSMISSION SYSTEM As at June 30, 2018' (SNGPLAR-2018.pdf, printed p.32-33) lists them as SEPARATE line items -- row 11 'SAWAN-QADIRPUR' 24in mainline 131.00 km (=P4079), and rows 12-17 a chain of 42in LOOPLINE segments explicitly named 'SAWAN CUSTODY TRANSFER POINT-SV1' -> 'SV1-SV2 LINE' (25.12) -> 'SV2-SV4 SEGMENT' (55.33) -> 'SV4-SV5' (20.92) -> 'SV5-QV1 SEGMENT' (29.40), summing to ~130.6-133.5 km depending on which custody-transfer stub is included -- an almost exact match to P4101's 130.77 km AND the literal source of the 'SV1'/'QV1' valve-station names in P4101's title. SNGPL's Annual Report 2017 'MILESTONES' timeline (printed p.52-53) is explicit that the 42in line is a NEW parallel augmentation, not the same pipe: 'PROJECT X (PHASE-I) ... 42"dia x 21.45 KM loop line ... was undertaken for AUGMENTATION OF EXISTING 24" dia Sawan-Qadirpur pipeline to transport future indigenous and imported gases' (i.e. the 42in loop was built alongside, not instead of, the 24in mainline). GEM's own wiki page for SV1-QV1 (read for lead only, not cited) independently describes its route as 'parallel to Sawan-Qadirpur', a third line of agreement. Two different diameters, two different vintages (this row ~2003 vs P4101 completed ~2015-2017 per the same milestone timeline), and an explicit company statement that one augments the other -- this is a mainline+capacity-loop pair, not a digitized duplicate.
